reason: The first live 4-arm run scored 44% of all failures as column_count_mismatch: the candidate returned the gold's rows under a different projection. The questions did not state what to return, so the gold's column list was unknowable. Each question below was rewritten to state the output shape it already implied. No gold SQL was changed by this revision.

revised.before: Which products have been discontinued?
revised.after: Which products have been discontinued? List each one's name, category and unit price.
revised.justification: "Which products" names no projection; the gold's three columns were unstated. Names the columns the gold already returns; the filter (NULL-means-active) is untouched.

revised.before: List the customers based in Texas.
revised.after: List the customers based in Texas, showing each customer's name and city.
revised.justification: "List the customers" does not say which customer attributes. States the gold's two; the 'TX' vs 'Texas' encoding difficulty is deliberately left in.

revised.before: What are our five most expensive products?
revised.after: What are our five most expensive products? Show the product name and its price.
revised.justification: "Most expensive" implies price is wanted but never says so; sort, limit and tie-break are unchanged.

revised.before: Which orders are still pending?
revised.after: Which orders are still pending? Give the order id and the date it was placed.
revised.justification: "Which orders" identifies no columns; states the gold's identifier plus date.

revised.before: Which customers signed up before June 2022?
revised.after: Which customers signed up before June 2022? Show their name and the date they signed up.
revised.justification: Adds the projection only. Phrased as 'the date they signed up' so the column name is still not handed over (the item's stated point).

revised.before: How many orders has each customer placed, including customers who haven't ordered anything?
revised.after: How many orders has each customer placed, including customers who haven't ordered anything? Show the customer id, name and order count.
revised.justification: The count was specified, the customer identification was not (id, name, or both). LEFT-JOIN difficulty untouched.

revised.before: Which product category brings in the most revenue from orders that were actually delivered?
revised.after: Which product category brings in the most revenue from orders that were actually delivered? Show the category and its revenue.
revised.justification: Asked for a category but the gold also returns the revenue that justifies it; states that second column.

revised.before: For each customer who has bought something, how many distinct products have they purchased?
revised.after: For each customer who has bought something, how many distinct products have they purchased? Show the customer id, name and the number of distinct products.
revised.justification: The measure was specified, the customer columns were not.

revised.before: Which products have sold at least 10 units in total?
revised.after: Which products have sold at least 10 units in total? Show the product id, name and total units sold.
revised.justification: "Which products" names no columns and does not say the unit total is wanted back; the HAVING threshold is unchanged.

revised.before: Which customers have never placed an order?
revised.after: Which customers have never placed an order? Give the customer id and name.
revised.justification: Anti-join difficulty untouched; only the two identifying columns are now stated.

revised.before: For every order, show how it ranks by recency (1 = most recent) among that same customer's orders.
revised.after: For every order, show the customer id, the order id, the order date, and how the order ranks by recency (1 = most recent) among that same customer's orders.
revised.justification: The rank was specified, the three columns it is reported against were not; RANK-vs-ROW_NUMBER and the partitioning are untouched.

revised.before: Which calendar month generated the most revenue from delivered orders?
revised.after: Which calendar month generated the most revenue from delivered orders? Show the month and its revenue.
revised.justification: Asked for a month but the gold also returns the revenue behind it; states that column.

revised.before: Among customers who have placed at least one order, which ones spent more than the average total spend for that group?
revised.after: Among customers who have placed at least one order, which ones spent more than the average total spend for that group? Show the customer id, name and total spend.
revised.justification: "Which ones" names no columns and does not say the total is wanted back; the above-average CTE pattern is untouched.

revised.before: For each product category, what share of total revenue does it represent?
revised.after: For each product category, show its revenue and what share of total revenue that represents.
revised.justification: "What share" implies one column; the gold also returns the revenue the share is computed from. States both.

revised.before: Which members have a lifetime membership that never expires?
revised.after: Which members have a lifetime membership that never expires? List their names.
revised.justification: "Which members" could be answered with any member attribute; the gold returns names only. The NULL-means-lifetime inference is untouched.

revised.before: Which books were published before 1990?
revised.after: Which books were published before 1990? Show the title and year of publication.
revised.justification: "Which books" names no columns; states the gold's two.

revised.before: For which authors do we not know a birth year?
revised.after: For which authors do we not know a birth year? List their names.
revised.justification: States that names alone are wanted; the NULL filter is untouched.

revised.before: Which loans are still out — not yet returned?
revised.after: Which loans are still out — not yet returned? Show the loan id, the book and member ids, and the date it is due.
revised.justification: "Which loans" names none of the gold's four columns.

revised.before: Which authors have written more than one book in our collection?
revised.after: Which authors have written more than one book in our collection? Show the author's name and how many books.
revised.justification: The threshold was specified, the returned count and the author column were not; the many-to-many join is untouched.

revised.before: For members who joined in 2020, is their membership still active as of the start of 2024?
revised.after: For members who joined in 2020, show their name, the date they joined, and their membership status as of the start of 2024 — 'lifetime', 'active' or 'expired'.
revised.justification: Names the three output columns and the status vocabulary, without saying which case maps to which — the NULL-is-a-third-case inference, the item's stated point, still has to be made by the model.

revised.before: Which books have been checked out more than five times?
revised.after: Which books have been checked out more than five times? Show the title and the number of loans.
revised.justification: The threshold was specified, the returned count and the book column were not.

revised.before: Which members have never checked out a single book?
revised.after: Which members have never checked out a single book? Give the member id and name.
revised.justification: Anti-join difficulty untouched; only the two identifying columns are now stated.

revised.before: For each member, what's their most recent checkout date, alongside their all-time loan count?
revised.after: For each member, show their member id, their most recent checkout date, and their all-time loan count.
revised.justification: Both measures were already specified; only the member identifier (id, not name) was not. Double-window difficulty untouched.

revised.before: List every subcategory that falls under Fiction, no matter how many levels deep.
revised.after: List every subcategory that falls under Fiction, no matter how many levels deep, showing each one's id and name.
revised.justification: The recursive walk was specified, the two output columns were not.

revised.before: Which members currently have more than one book overdue (due before June 2024 and still not returned)?
revised.after: Which members currently have more than one book overdue (due before June 2024 and still not returned)? Show the member id and how many overdue books they have.
revised.justification: The overdue definition and threshold are untouched; the member column and the returned count are now stated.

revised.before: For each category that has books, what fraction of its books were published in the last ten years covered by our catalog (2014-2023)?
revised.after: For each category that has books, show the category name, how many of its books were published in the last ten years covered by our catalog (2014-2023), how many books it has in total, and the fraction that is recent.
revised.justification: "What fraction" implies one column; the gold returns four. States all four, leaving the correlated-subquery structure untouched.

revised.before: Which users are on the enterprise plan?
revised.after: Which users are on the enterprise plan? Show their username and country.
revised.justification: "Which users" names no columns; states the gold's two.

revised.before: List all churn events, most recent first.
revised.after: List all churn events, most recent first, showing the event id, the user id and when it happened.
revised.justification: The sort was specified, the three columns were not.

revised.before: Which users signed up in November 2023?
revised.after: Which users signed up in November 2023? Show the username and the date they signed up.
revised.justification: "Which users" names no columns; states the gold's two.

revised.before: What are the ten most recent purchase events?
revised.after: What are the ten most recent purchase events? Show the event id, the user id, when it happened and the revenue.
revised.justification: Filter, sort and limit were specified; the four columns were not.

revised.before: What's the total purchase revenue generated by each user?
revised.after: What's the total purchase revenue generated by each user? Show the user id and their total revenue.
revised.justification: "Each user" left the identifier open (id or username). The cents-vs-dollars question is deliberately left open — under D13 that is a domain corrective's job, not the question's.

revised.before: Which users have made at least three purchases?
revised.after: Which users have made at least three purchases? Show the user id and their purchase count.
revised.justification: The boundary-inclusive threshold is untouched; the identifier and the returned count are now stated.

revised.before: Which users have never triggered a single event?
revised.after: Which users have never triggered a single event? Give the user id and username.
revised.justification: Anti-join difficulty untouched; only the two identifying columns are now stated.

revised.before: For each user, what was their single largest purchase?
revised.after: For each user, what was their single largest purchase? Show the user id, the event id, when it happened and the amount.
revised.justification: States the four columns only. The tie at the maximum — RANK keeps both rows, ROW_NUMBER keeps one — is the item's documented difficulty and is deliberately NOT resolved.

revised.before: Show the running cumulative total of purchase revenue over time, across all users.
revised.after: Show the running cumulative total of purchase revenue over time, across all users — for each purchase, when it happened, its revenue and the running total.
revised.justification: The running total was specified, the two columns it is reported against were not.

revised.before: Which signup month had the most new users, and how did it compare to the month before it?
revised.after: Which signup month had the most new users, and how many signed up in the month before it? Show the month, its signups and the previous month's signups.
revised.justification: "How did it compare" left the shape open (a delta? a ratio?); states the gold's three columns. The LAG and top-1 pick are untouched.

revised.before: Which users made a purchase within 24 hours of their signup event?
revised.after: Which users made a purchase within 24 hours of their signup event? List their user ids.
revised.justification: "Which users" could be answered with a username; states that the id alone is wanted. The 24-hour window arithmetic is untouched.

revised.before: Which plans have more than five distinct users who made at least one purchase?
revised.after: Which plans have more than five distinct users who made at least one purchase? Show the plan and how many such users it has.
revised.justification: The threshold and de-duplication are untouched; the returned count is now stated.

reviewed_unchanged.why: "How many events of each type" already determines (type, count).
"Total purchase revenue by country" already determines (country, revenue).
"Average purchase size for each plan tier" already determines (plan, average).
"What are the names of our top-level categories" already says names, and nothing else.

"How many books in each category" already determines (category, count). Left alone deliberately although it is ill-posed in a different way — whether a category with zero books should appear — because fixing that would change which rows are correct, not the output shape; recorded as a known open defect.
"On average how many copies per category" already determines (category, average). Its remaining failure mode is rounding, not projection; recorded as a known open defect.
"Total revenue by product category" already determines (category, revenue): a grouped aggregate names both its grouping key and its measure.
